No result exists yet, so equivalence is neither shown nor claimed.", "artifacts": [{"kind": "equivalence_report", "title": "Equivalence report: gray_counter.v (gold) vs gray_counter_refactor.v (gate)", "summary": "This report serves [requirement:req-5de0de52be]: verify the existing Gray-code counter with an equivalence check of its refactor. Gold is the approved [artifact:prj-675bd09855.design-under-test.a1] gray_counter.v. Gate is the approved [artifact:prj-675bd09855.design-under-test.a2] gray_counter_refactor.v. The two designs share the module name gray_counter, the ports clk, rst, en, gray[3:0] and wrap, and the state register gray[3:0]. Gold finds the next code by decoding to binary, adding one and re-encoding; its wrap flag is en && gray==4'b1000. Gate finds the next code by the parity flip rule; its wrap flag is en & gray[3] & ~|gray[2:0]. Both use a synchronous reset to 4'b0000 and hold the count when en is low. The setup gray_counter_equiv.eqy reads each version with read_verilog, elaborates both with prep -top gray_counter, and proves partitions with a single sby strategy using the smtbmc engine at depth 20. The register partition uses sby because sat can pass a wrong register design. Only one strategy is listed and it has no timeout, so no weaker strategy can take over a partition. Status: pending. No equivalence.run result is cited, so no verdict is given. The independent upstream review of the RTL is recorded as [evidence:prj-675bd09855.design-under-test.e1]. Equivalence compares the two versions only; it does not check either one against the specification."}], "files": [{"path": "gray_counter_equiv.eqy", "kind": "equivalence_setup", "title": "eqy setup: gray_counter gold vs refactor gate", "summary": "This setup compares [artifact:prj-675bd09855.design-under-test.a1] (gold, gray_counter.v) with [artifact:prj-675bd09855.design-under-test.a2] (gate, gray_counter_refactor.v), for [requirement:req-5de0de52be]. Each side reads its own file by a relative name and elaborates with prep -top gray_counter. The [gold] and [gate] command lists differ because they read different files. All commands are on the allow list. One sby strategy is used: engine smtbmc, depth 20, no timeout and no option lines.", "entry": "gray_counter"}], "tool_runs": [], "claims": ["The gold and refactored gray_counter are expected to be equivalent at gray[3:0] and wrap. This is a reading of the RTL, not a tool result.", "Both versions name the state register gray, so eqy is expected to match it by name without [match] rules. This is an expectation, not something observed.", "Depth 20 exceeds the 16 states of the 4-bit register. This was chosen as a margin; it is not a measured requirement."], "escalation": null, "notes": "There is no tool run to cite. The platform runs equivalence.run over gray_counter_equiv.eqy, with the approved rtl_source files placed beside it. Please read the gold and gate file names and the proved-partition count from that result. Mutation testing of this setup (for example a wrong wrap condition or a wrong flip bit in the gate) is the reviewer's step; this seat cannot do it. If the platform rejects the bare 'engine smtbmc' line, the fallback is 'engine smtbmc yices'."}
=== FILE: gray_counter_equiv.eqy ===
[gold]
read_verilog gray_counter.v
prep -top gray_counter

[gate]
read_verilog gray_counter_refactor.v
prep -top gray_counter

[strategy sby]
use sby
depth 20
engine smtbmc
=== END FILE ===
